newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Sheu appeal helps nudge Taiwan money rates higher.
newsitem.headline: Sheu appeal helps nudge Taiwan money rates higher.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates were firmer at midday on Wednesday, reflecting central bank Governor Sheu Yuan-dong's comment on Tuesday that the overnight interbank rate was too low, dealers said.
The interbank rate rose to 4.991 percent from Tuesday's 4.568 close, with the 30-day commercial paper at 4.75-4.85 percent against 4.60-4.70.
Dealers said they expected rates to edge toward 5.00 percent but did not expect major gains as liquidity in the banking system remained loose.
Sheu had said he hoped the overnight money rate would rise to five percent, saying investors' interests would be hurt if liquidity became too loose.
Government bond yields fell slightly on Wednesda morning, with the 10-year 84/1 at 5.7325-7400, the seven-year was at 5.4750 and the 10-year 86/1 at 5.8000.
Traders expected bond yields to remain in a consolidation phase in coming sessions.
